subject: On‑prem deployment: operator visibility & customer keystore policy proposal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem deployment: operator visibility & customer keystore policy proposal

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time earlier. As we discussed, Meditex wants an on‑prem (air‑gapped / VPC) private deployment with the following high‑level constraints: customer‑controlled keys, minimal operator visibility into call metadata, and clear subprocessors and transfer controls in the DPA. I attached a short proposal that maps Redwood's operational controls to your requirements.

Key points in the attached: 
- Customer keystore model: customer provides KMS keys; Redwood runs with an operator role that cannot decrypt customer payloads.
- Operator telemetry: only aggregated health and agent‑state metrics are visible; request‑level logs are held by Meditex unless the customer opts in for support‑share.
- Breakglass: emergency support flow with audited, time‑limited access and joint approval from both parties.
- Subprocessor list for on‑prem installs (agents, monitoring connectors) and proposed contractual gating.

Can you confirm whether the telemetry granularity is acceptable (we list examples in page 2 of the PDF), and whether your legal team needs any additional language around escrow / key‑recovery? If Meditex would prefer a formal escrow arrangement rather than a runbook, we can surface options.

If this looks reasonable I’ll loop in Marissa and Grace to prepare a DPA appendix and a short mutual action plan for procurement.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 415‑555‑0127

Attachments: redwood-privdep-keystore-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf); meditex-dataflow-diagram.png (image/png)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@meditex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Eve Robinson <eve.robinson@meditex.com>, security@meditex.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On‑prem deployment: operator visibility & customer keystore policy proposal

Irene —

Appreciate the quick write‑up. A few follow ups from our side after reviewing the PDF: 
1) Telemetry: the examples are helpful. We need explicit guarantees that PII or PHI will never be present in any telemetry payload (we understand aggregate health is fine). Can you add a line committing to stripping any PII/PHI before it leaves the appliance?
2) Breakglass: Meditex prefers escrow over a live breakglass unless we can bind access to a signed request with step‑up auth and an independent auditor present.
3) Subprocessors: your list includes a monitoring agent; does that agent do any packet inspection or content‑level indexing? We expect the monitoring agent to be metadata‑only.

Eve (procurement) — could you confirm timelines and whether legal will want to propose redlines to the DPA once we have the appendix?

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Security, Meditex Health

Hi Samir —

Thanks — a couple clarifications from the ops/security engineering side: 
- Telemetry pipeline: the appliance ships with a configurable telemetry filter. By default it sends only anonymized counters, host health, and resource consumption. We will add a contractual clause to explicitly prohibit PHI/PII in telemetry and to require Redwood to destroy any accidental capture within 24 hours and notify Meditex.
- Monitoring agent: it does not perform DPI or content indexing. It's a metadata agent (process/CPU/memory, host reachability, process crash reports). We will provide the agent’s manifest and minimal config in the appendix so Meditex can validate.
- Breakglass / escrow: we prefer a dual‑path model: primary — customer‑controlled escrow (a sealed key share model you control); secondary — time‑boxed breakglass requiring 2 internal Redwood approvers + customer approval and full audit. We're happy to document both and let legal pick.

Ben and Marissa — can you prep a short DPA appendix and a procurement timeline (2 weeks for review + 1 week for signatures is our estimate) so Samir/Eve have something to work with?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Cloud Operations
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
